# Introduction

The **`ihcheterogeneity`** analysis (IHC Heterogeneity Analysis) provides clinicopathological researchers and biostatisticians with intuitive, publication-ready tools in jamovi and R.

## Key Capabilities

- **Reference-based design** (whole section, hotspot or overall score supplied in `wholesection`):
  computes the Spearman rank correlation of each region with the reference (with Fisher-$z$ 95% CIs
  using the Bonett & Wright 2000 variance), the absolute-agreement ICC(2,1) and consistency ICC(3,1)
  with F-based 95% CIs (McGraw & Wong 1996), the within-case coefficient of variation (root mean
  square of per-case CVs across the reference and regions), and for each region (plus the mean of
  all regions) the mean difference from the reference with its 95% CI, Hedges' $g$, and Bland-Altman
  95% limits of agreement with approximate 95% CIs (Bland & Altman 1999).
- **Inter-regional design** (no reference supplied): computes pairwise Spearman correlations with
  Bonett & Wright (2000) 95% CIs, inter-regional ICC(2,1)/ICC(3,1), within-case CV across regions,
  and all pairwise regional differences with Fieller percentage-difference CIs and Bland-Altman LoAs.
- **Equivalence, material bias, and proportional bias**: each systematic difference is judged against
  a user-specified margin (`bias_margin`, default 5% of the comparison mean) using Fieller intervals:
  ruled out when its 90% CI lies inside the margin (two one-sided tests, Schuirmann 1987), shown to
  be material when a Bonferroni-adjusted CI lies entirely beyond it, and inconclusive otherwise.
  Proportional bias (whether the difference changes with the biomarker level) is tested using
  heteroscedasticity-robust HC3 standard errors (MacKinnon & White 1985) and the Krouwer (2008)
  three-slope rule across both measurements and their mean so unequal measurement precision alone
  does not trigger false proportional-bias warnings.
- **Ordinal / coarsely binned score guard**: integer scores such as HER2 (`0-3+`) or Allred (`0, 2-8`)
  are automatically detected and marked `"Not graded: ordinal or binned values"` rather than graded
  by CVs or 5% continuous equivalence margins.
- **Optional analyses**: two-way random-effects variance components (`variance_components`), sample-size
  planning for ICC precision (`sample_size_planning`, Bonett 2002), and spatial compartment comparisons
  (`compareCompartments`, `compartmentTests`).

# Example Workflow in R

```r
library(ClinicoPath)

data("ihcheterogeneity_test", package = "ClinicoPath")

ihcheterogeneity(
  data = ihcheterogeneity_test,
  wholesection = "wholesection",
  biopsy1 = "biopsy1",
  biopsy2 = "biopsy2",
  biopsy3 = "biopsy3",
  biopsy4 = "biopsy4",
  spatial_id = "spatial_id",
  bias_margin = 5,
  compareCompartments = TRUE,
  showReportSentences = TRUE
)
```

# Clinical & Statistical Interpretation

The Clinical Assessment gives one verdict: agreement thresholds met (every systematic difference
ruled out within the margin), met but not confirmed, moderate, inadequate, not adequate for
substitution (a material systematic difference), or insufficient data. Choose the correlation
threshold, the CV threshold and the margin before looking at the results. The results describe
the cases analysed; they are not an external validation.
